dct_description_sm: Paalliq valley, in Kovik Bay, located in north of Akulivik (Nunavik, Qubec) was studied as part of a collaborative project, university-community. Geomorphological and geoarcheological fieldworks were conducted during summer 2015 complementary to archeological surveys and inventories led by the Avataq Cultural Institute. About twenty Thule/Inuit sod houses were found in the east limit of Paalliq  valley. According to our preliminary results, theses houses were built on a Dorset site. Extra-site geoarchaeological investigations aim to document the geomorphological context in which Dorset and Thule occupied Paalliq 1 valley, in relation to postglacial marine regression (linked to isostatic rebound) and climate change. Intra-site geoarchaeological studies undertaken in a multifamilial sod house, (Structure 10) aim to identify cultural and natural processes of site formation (biopedologic and sedimentary processes). The main research hypothesis is that this house would have been occupied successively by the Dorset and Thule; the latter would have caused reorganization of the site (anthropoturbation).
